title: Website chat on a Sunday night: a noise, one question, the assistant hands over, the junior operator next morning
demonstrates: The assistant answers first on the web chat, from public pages only. The customer is unclear (R13): she asks what it costs to fix a noise she hears mostly in the morning. The assistant asks once, braking or turning, and that settles it. It cannot book, so it takes a name and a number and hands over as a scheduling request. The junior operator picks it up six minutes after opening.

scenario.who_writes: A first-time customer, on her phone, after the shops have closed.
scenario.wants: She thinks she wants a price to fix a noise. What she needs is a brake inspection, soon.
scenario.what_happens: One clarifying question, a photo of the dash, the public price of an inspection, a request for Tuesday morning. The assistant cannot book: it asks for her name, number and shop, hands over, and says somebody will get back to her. Monday at 7:36 Maya books Tuesday 9:00 and says she will call to confirm (the call is in the calls set, unscored).

timeline.text: hi how much to fix a noise my car is making

Hi! I'm the assistant for Brennan Auto Care. The shops are closed right now and open at 7:30 tomorrow, but I can help in the meantime. A price depends on where the noise comes from, so one question first: do you hear it when you press the brake, or when you turn the steering wheel? And what kind of car is it?
when i brake. like a scraping
idk if it matters but theres a light on now too

files.shows: instrument cluster at night, the red BRAKE lamp lit

timeline.text: Thank you for the photo: that's the red BRAKE warning light. I can't diagnose a car over chat, but a scraping sound when you press the brake, together with that light, should be looked at soon, and I wouldn't put many miles on it until then. The first step is a brake inspection, which is $49.95. The technician shows you what they find before any repair is priced. Would you like me to ask the shop to get you in?
yes please. can i bring it tuesday morning before work? its a 2014 crv

I can't book a time myself, but I'll pass your request to the service desk and they'll confirm it with you. What's your name and the best number to reach you? And which shop works better: East Main Street or Bonny Oaks Drive?
Thank you, Rachel. Your request is with the team now, and somebody will get back to you as soon as possible. Anything else I can help with tonight?

Wants a brake inspection on Tuesday morning before work, East Main Street.

facts: first written at 21:10 on the evening before day A, outside opening hours
one clarifying question, asked by the assistant
the assistant named only the inspection price, 49.95, and no repair
handed over with her name and number; the contact itself holds neither
slot 6's first line 6.7 working minutes after opening

why: The assistant never books, never quotes a repair, never promises a time: 'as soon as possible' is the product's own sentence.
One question is enough here: it offers two readings, and her answer comes with a photo. The hand-off note says what was asked and how she answered.
Maya's two lines are her sheet: complete, a time offered before anything else, one exclamation mark, and the second is the draft sent as it was.
